name: Ravine Stalker

special_abilities.name: Ambush Predator
special_abilities.desc: The stalker has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it has surprised. Ravine Stalkers hunt in family groups of three, coordinating drop-ambushes from rock faces above a ravine or canyon trail.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.desc: The stalker makes two attacks: one with its bite and one with its claw.

actions.name: Bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 13 (2d8 + 4) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing damage, and if the target is Large or smaller, it is grappled (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the stalker can't claw another target.

actions.name: Crush
actions.desc: The stalker crushes a creature it is grappling. The target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 18 (4d8) bludgeoning damage. Half as much damage on a successful save. This action can only be used against a creature the stalker is currently grappling.

source: Homebrew — native to Fol. Large, dark, territorial predators that hunt in family groups of three, coordinating drop-ambushes from rock faces onto prey below.

name: Greyback

special_abilities.name: Thick Hide
special_abilities.desc: The greyback's pale, cold-adapted hide is resistant to piercing and slashing damage — edged weapons bite far less deeply than blunt force or fire. Its hide also makes it highly resistant to cold.

special_abilities.name: Snow Camouflage
special_abilities.desc: The greyback has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to hide in snowy or icy terrain.

special_abilities.name: Ambush Predator
special_abilities.desc: The greyback has advantage on attack rolls against any creature it has surprised. Greybacks den in ice caves and ambush from rock faces above.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.desc: The greyback makes three attacks: one with its bite and two with its claws.

actions.name: Bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 16 (2d10 + 5) piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +9 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 12 (2d6 + 5) slashing damage.

source: Homebrew — native to Fol. Pale, territorial cave hunters that den in ice caves and ambush from rock faces. Elite-tier predators; their cold-resistant hide shrugs off edged weapons far better than blunt force or fire.

name: Sarnach

special_abilities.name: Flyby
special_abilities.desc: The sarnach doesn't provoke an opportunity attack when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

actions.name: Bite
actions.desc: Melee Weapon Attack: +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit: 6 (2d4 + 1) piercing damage.

source: Homebrew — native to Orvath. Stat block based on the Pteranodon (Monster Manual); the description below is campaign lore.
description:
A pale, heat-shimmer-colored raptor native only to the Orvath region and nowhere else — larger than any lowland eagle, and the animal the region's entire falconry culture (and, indirectly, its banking economy) is built around.

Hunts by reading thermals and mirage-distortion most creatures can't parse at all — a sense tied to the region's harsh day-to-night temperature swing and thin, dry air, not something that transplants to a lowland raptor. Clans bond one sarnach per generation per family, sometimes for life; a bonded pair is a serious, rare thing, not a casual working relationship.

A trained sarnach isn't valuable primarily as a hunting bird. Its real worth is that it can spot a distant desert storm rolling in long before any human eye can — and in Orvath, a storm means a fresh strike of duskglass (lightning-fused sand with a latent magical-anchoring property found nowhere else) somewhere out in the waste, up for grabs to whichever clan gets there first. A clan's standing, wealth, and leverage over the settled city is downstream of how good their sarnach is. See the lore entry "duskglass-001" for the full duskglass economy this feeds.
